content.title: About
content.content: A prepackaged vanilla ice cream cone is a convenient dessert ready to eat. Inside the crisp waffle cone lies smooth, creamy vanilla ice cream with a natural vanilla flavor, finished with a thin crunchy shell.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vanilla is one of the most popular ice cream flavors worldwide.
The waffle cone was invented in the early 1900s in the United States as a handy way to serve ice cream.
Prepackaged cones often contain a small amount of air to prevent deformation during transport.
There are over 30 flavor variations for ice cream cones, but vanilla remains a classic.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The dairy base of the ice cream provides calcium, essential for bone health.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D present in dairy helps with calcium absorption.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Ice cream supplies fast‑acting carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat for quick energy.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Ice cream contains lactose, which may cause discomfort for those who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to casein or whey proteins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The cone can be eaten straight from the package. For extra flavor, add toppings such as chocolate sauce, nuts, berries, or sprinkle with cookie crumbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once opened, consume within 1–2 days to avoid ice crystal formation and texture loss.
